descriptionChirho: Used adverbially to express simultaneity or accompaniment without governing a noun in the dative — 'at the same time,' 'together,' 'simultaneously.' Multilingual evidence: Spanish 'juntamente/al mismo tiempo,' Hindi 'साथही' (sāth-hī, simultaneously), Arabic 'مَعاً' (together, simultaneously), Korean '동시에/함께' (dongsie = at the same time), Swahili 'wakati huo huo/pamoja' (at that very time / together). Found in contexts expressing concurrent events or shared temporal reference (e.g., 1 Tim 5:13; Philem 1:22; Acts 24:26; 27:40).

Used as a preposition governing the dative case to mean 'together with,' expressing accompaniment of persons. Syntactically distinct from the adverbial use because it requires a dependent noun. Multilingual evidence: Spanish 'junto con/juntamente,' Hindi 'के साथ' (-ke sāth, with), Arabic 'مَعَ' (maʿa, with — the prepositional form), Korean '함께' (hamkke, together with), Swahili 'pamoja na' (together with, using the associative 'na'). Found in 1 Thess 4:17 and 5:10, both expressing believers being 'together with' the Lord.
